The bare "On day 8/10/14/17/23" series in the same Case report paragraph uses one day count and orders its own events; "from day 5" (prone ventilation) sits in the earlier paragraph next to "the third/fourth/fifth day after ECMO" and is not shown to share that count, so it is not ordered against either series.
A bronchopleural fistula is stated as part of the initial diagnosis, but after ECMO and PEEP increases the text says a BPF "was suspected".

The five blood gas sets, the HFOV settings and the dyspnea changes are described in sequence, but only set 5 states a time (1 h after the interventions); the source does not state intervals between the other sets or link each gas set to a named time.

The Discussion says that the patient was treated with VA-ECMO but also describes veno-venous ECMO and "awake ECMO" in general terms, and calls the fistula "BPT" once; these Discussion sentences are not recorded as extra patient facts.
The Discussion states "Later, when we lowered PEEP, the pneumothorax improved", but the Case report never describes a PEEP reduction; it describes extubation on day 8.

The "after intubation" anchor for the 12 h and 24 h chest x-rays does not say which intubation (the restart of ventilator-assisted ventilation or another) it refers to; no order with the preceding events is recorded.

The Introduction and abstract call the pneumothorax spontaneous, whereas the Case report diagnoses meconium aspiration syndrome complicated by BPF and attributes persistence of the BPF to positive pressure ventilation.

The Figure 4 and Figure 6 captions state findings (left exudative pleural effusion; improved exudative lesions in both lungs) that the case text does not state; the captions give no time, and the text sentences citing these figures do not time the caption-only findings.
